tasks.short: Handle receipts, petty cash, bookkeeping and routine banking transactions.

steps.what: Receive payments, count cash and issue receipts.
Enter receipts and cash movements into the {ERP} or petty cash register.
Compare cash and bank transactions with receipts; investigate differences.
Prepare payment batches and cash deposit details from approved requests.
Check payees, amounts and authority; approve and release electronic payments.
Securely deposit cash or hand over authorised petty cash.
Post confirmations and file supporting receipts in the {ERP}.

tasks.design: Configure receipt capture, matching and payment preparation in the {ERP}, with authorised release in the {BANK}. A small integration attaches confirmations and cash movement receipts to the ledger and sends unmatched items to a queue in the {WORKFLOW}. Cash handling and payment approval remain human actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cash evidence, payment requests and bank confirmations sit in separate places. Small transaction volumes often made integration costs unattractive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing matching and approval features can cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building the remaining connectors and validation rules.
tasks.still_hard: Physical cash, disputed receipts and changed payee details require care. Bank permissions and separation of duties must remain intact.
tasks.human_edge: Notice suspicious requests, explain discrepancies and take responsibility for physical money.

ambition.what: A daily cash discrepancy review before the next payment run

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time entering transactions and more time resolving cash discrepancies. They can propose corrections and pause suspect requests; payment authority does not increase automatically.

reach.task: Review cash handling arrangements across office locations.
reach.learn: Cash controls, custody arrangements and approval limits.

reach.task: Identify recurring causes of unmatched receipts.
reach.learn: Reconciliation categories and basic process analysis.

evidence.claim: Receipt capture, bank matching and payment approval are established finance-system capabilities.
Physical cash custody and payment authority limit the share that can become unattended.

assumptions: This is a cash-handling office; cash work may be much smaller elsewhere.
The time shares describe a mixed transaction cycle, including finance approval.
The {ERP} supports matching and payment batches.
Duplicate entry disappears only after receipt capture becomes the source record.
Build ranges cover one office and one bank connection.
unknowns: Actual cash volume and payment methods.
Available {ERP} and {BANK} interfaces and licences.
Payment limits, signatory rules and cash custody procedures.
Who may amend payee records.
Applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Can receipt capture create ledger entries without a separate register?
Can the bank connection preserve approval limits and duplicate-payment protection?
Which discrepancy categories account for most investigation time?
new_work: Review unmatched transactions and rejected batches.
Maintain matching rules and connector credentials.
Check that confirmations reconcile to released payments.
Test payee-change controls after configuration changes.
tasks.statement: Collect, count, and disburse money, do basic bookkeeping, and complete banking transactions.

tasks.short: Answer questions, explain information, record orders and help resolve complaints.

steps.what: Listen to the person and clarify their question, order or complaint.
Find approved information and relevant account, order or case records.
Write a response using the retrieved information.

loop.input: Clarified free-text request and access-filtered response facts with source references.
loop.output: Response draft with cited facts and explicit unanswered questions.
loop.check: Check source references, amounts and identifiers against retrieved records; the clerk checks meaning and tone.
loop.stop: One draft and at most one revision per request; missing sources or failed checks return to manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use templates for standard questions. Varied wording and explanations need a bounded drafting loop.

steps.what: Explain the answer, respond to follow-up questions and check understanding.
Enter order details and confirm the customer's instructions.
Send the accepted order confirmation.
Discuss the complaint and propose a remedy or escalation.
Approve a remedy outside the clerk's delegated limits.
Send the complaint outcome and update the case.

tasks.design: An access-controlled answer desk joins approved material in the {DOCS} with permitted records from the {CRM}, {ERP} and {HELPDESK}. Templates answer standard questions; one bounded loop drafts varied explanations for clerk review, while configured order forms and outcome templates handle paperwork. People retain the conversation and approve orders, exceptional remedies and complaint notices at their action points.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding current facts required several searches. Unstructured questions did not fit fixed templates, and complaints needed personal judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Connectors and template generators are cheaper to build with AI-assisted coding. Bounded drafting can use retrieved facts without granting independent decision authority.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting policies, identity checks and contractual promises need care. A fluent draft can still misstate what the company may offer.
tasks.human_edge: Understand what the person needs, explain limits respectfully and repair trust after a failure.

ambition.what: A daily review of recurring complaint causes with the service manager.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time searching and composing routine paperwork, leaving more time for explanation and complaint follow-up. They can recommend service changes; remedy limits require explicit delegation.

reach.task: Identify recurring inquiry and complaint causes.
reach.learn: Consistent case coding, process mapping and separating patterns from isolated incidents.

reach.task: Improve escalation and delegated remedy procedures.
reach.learn: Service policy, approval thresholds and complaint review.

evidence.claim: Record lookup, order forms and confirmation templates can use deterministic technology.
Source-grounded drafting can assist varied explanations while people retain consequential decisions.
GDPR and EU AI Act obligations depend on data processing and intended use; these are not automatically employment decisions.

assumptions: The steps cover question, order and complaint branches; not every request follows all branches.
The step involving the service manager includes approval time within the end-to-end task.
Routine orders are within the clerk's delegated authority.
An accepted order can trigger a fixed confirmation without a second approval.
The assistant cannot grant remedies, change policy or send free-text drafts independently.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Which policies are authoritative and who updates them?
What order and remedy authority does the clerk have?
Which systems permit record lookup and validated writes?
What identity checks apply to customer and employee inquiries?
Which GDPR requirements and national consultation rules apply to the proposed processing?
research_questions: Which inquiry types fit templates without a model?
Can draft checks detect unsupported promises and incorrect record references?
Does the intended use introduce an EU AI Act high-risk use case?
new_work: Review varied drafts and handle missing or conflicting sources.
Maintain policy versions, templates and escalation limits.
Test factual accuracy and recipient access.
Review recurring complaint causes with the service manager.
Maintain GDPR retention and access controls and assess EU AI Act requirements for the actual use.
tasks.statement: Communicate with customers, employees, and other individuals to answer questions, disseminate or explain information, take orders, and address complaints.

tasks.short: Answer calls, find the right recipient, transfer callers and pass on messages.

steps.what: Greet the caller and establish their purpose.
Look up the department, contact details and availability.
Choose a recipient or decide to take a message.
Transfer the caller and check that the connection succeeds.
Record and confirm the caller's name, number, message and urgency when needed.
Send the confirmed message to the recipient.

tasks.design: Configure a searchable contact directory, routing buttons and failed-transfer fallback in the {TELEPHONY}, using permitted availability from the {CALENDAR}. A structured message form in the {WORKFLOW} sends confirmed messages through the {EMAIL} or {CHAT}; callers can still reach the clerk directly.
tasks.previous_blocker: Directories were stale and availability was scattered. Clerks copied messages between notes and mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing routing and form features cover the core changes. Small connectors can now be built and maintained more cheaply.
tasks.still_hard: Call purpose can be ambiguous. Distressed callers, confidential requests and absent recipients need human handling.
tasks.human_edge: Put callers at ease, recognise urgency and avoid disclosing information to the wrong person.

ambition.what: An acknowledged callback queue for callers who cannot reach a recipient.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time searching and forwarding notes, and more time resolving difficult routing. They gain discretion to prioritise callbacks within agreed limits.

reach.task: Coordinate callbacks and cover arrangements for unavailable colleagues.
reach.learn: Availability rules, escalation paths and clear message writing.

evidence.claim: Directories, transfer rules, structured message forms and notifications can be configured without a model.
Keeping caller confirmation avoids relying on unverified speech transcription for names and numbers.

assumptions: Step shares average transferred calls and message-taking calls; each caller does not follow both branches.
The clerk remains the main telephone contact.
The design does not require call recording or speech transcription.
Directory and message handling offer clearer gains than automating the human conversation.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Which routing and form features are already licensed?
Who maintains recipient and cover information?
Which calls need identity checks or immediate escalation?
Which availability fields may the clerk access?
Do national rules require employee consultation?
research_questions: Where do failed transfers and missed callbacks arise?
Can existing configuration provide the complete message workflow?
new_work: Maintain directories and cover arrangements.
Handle failed notifications and overdue callbacks.
Review access and retention for personal contact details under GDPR.
Check the EU AI Act implications if speech processing is added later.
tasks.statement: Answer telephones, direct calls, and take messages.

tasks.short: Compile, classify and file office records so colleagues can retrieve reliable information.

steps.what: Collect electronic records and attachments for filing.
Check completeness, duplicates and conflicting versions.
Assign record categories, reference numbers and access groups.

loop.input: Unmatched document text and an approved category list.
loop.output: Suggested category and supporting text; access comes from deterministic rules.
loop.check: Validate category, references and supporting text; default unresolved access to restricted.
loop.stop: One classification attempt per unmatched record; ambiguity or missing evidence goes to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sender and template rules cover standard records; varied free text needs limited interpretation.

steps.what: Save records in their designated locations with approved metadata.
Update the separate filing index with record locations.

tasks.design: Connect the {EMAIL} and {DOCS} to a records queue in the {WORKFLOW}, with duplicate checks and filing rules. A bounded classifier suggests categories for unmatched documents; approved metadata drives filing in the {DOCS}, whose searchable index replaces the separate {SPREADSHEET}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inconsistent naming, duplicate copies and unclear access rules made unattended filing unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing metadata and access controls handle standard records. AI-assisted coding reduces connector effort, while bounded classification covers unfamiliar text.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting originals, retention exceptions and sensitive access decisions require accountable people. GDPR limits copying and retention of personal records.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise which record is authoritative and resolve ownership disputes with the people involved.

ambition.what: A missing-record alert service for project closeout.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time resolving missing or conflicting evidence and less time moving files. They gain authority to return incomplete submissions under agreed acceptance rules; access-policy authority stays with record owners.

reach.task: Prepare project records for retention review.
reach.learn: Retention schedules, record provenance and legal-hold escalation.

evidence.claim: Scanning business post and turning forms into data is available today.
Paperbox organises insurance emails and attachments into case files; this supports feasibility, not general-office accuracy.
Metadata rules, duplicate checks and permission-controlled filing can handle standard records without an autonomous agent.

assumptions: The baseline includes a separate filing index; where absent, its time belongs to metadata maintenance.
Most records arrive digitally; substantial physical archives would add scanning and handling.
Build ranges cover one department and two connectors, including access approval and any applicable consultation.
The design preserves source records and does not automate deletion.
unknowns: Record volumes, formats and proportion of physical originals.
Available interfaces and existing metadata quality.
Who can approve categories, access groups and retention exceptions.
Applicable national rules for employee consultation and whether the deployment triggers them.
research_questions: How accurately can existing metadata rules classify a representative record sample?
Which exception categories benefit from text classification after deterministic rules are exhausted?
new_work: Review ambiguous categories and conflicting record versions.
Maintain category mappings and connector credentials.
Sample filed records for retrieval quality and access errors.
Resolve failed imports and missing-record alerts.
tasks.statement: Compile, copy, sort, and file records of office activities, business transactions, and other activities.

tasks.short: Complete, check and dispatch bills, contracts, policies, invoices and occasional payment documents.

steps.what: Retrieve recipient details, approved terms and document instructions.
Complete the appropriate template and attach supporting documents.
Check names, amounts, dates, attachments and template version.
Approve binding terms and sign documents requiring authorisation.
Send routine invoices and bills through the approved electronic channel.
Dispatch signed contracts and approved policy documents.
Print, envelope and post documents requiring paper delivery.
File final copies and update dispatch status.

tasks.design: Fill approved templates from the {ERP}, {CLM} and {DOCS}, then validate fields and attachments before dispatch. Routine bills leave through the {ERP}; binding documents require signatory approval through the {ESIGN} before release. Store delivery evidence automatically and generate print packs for necessary paper delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recipient records, terms and templates have different owners. Clerks bridge those gaps by copying fields and checking each document.
tasks.enabler_now: Template, signature and dispatch features already exist. Small connectors and explicit validation rules can now be built with less effort.
tasks.still_hard: Nonstandard terms, recipient changes and legally required delivery methods need judgement. A generator cannot resolve ambiguous authority.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a routine document creates an unusual commitment and obtain the right approval.

ambition.what: A document delivery status desk for internal requesters

tasks.altitude: The clerk handles incomplete requests, delivery failures and document exceptions instead of assembling every pack. They can return deficient requests and report delivery status; signing authority stays with the authorised role.

reach.task: Prepare contract signature packs.
reach.learn: Document versions, signature authority and delivery evidence.

reach.task: Maintain final document records.
reach.learn: Metadata, retention schedules and access permissions.

evidence.claim: CHILI GraFx fills governed layout templates, supporting the template-generation building block.
Structured records and approved templates can generate routine office documents without a model loop.

assumptions: The steps describe a mixed queue; billing, contract and paper branches are conditional.
Most documents use approved templates and structured source records.
Approval time is counted in s4; s6 consumes that approval without another review.
Paper dispatch uses documents already cleared for release.
Checks are uncommon; any payment instrument requires the banking controls described in the money-handling task.
Build ranges cover a small initial template set.
unknowns: Document volumes and the actual paper share.
Which documents require signatures or proof of delivery.
Template ownership and approval limits.
Whether recipient records have a reliable source.
Available dispatch and signature interfaces.
research_questions: Which document families can use existing template configuration?
Can dispatch retries avoid duplicate invoices and duplicate contract sends?
Which delivery evidence must be retained for each document family?
new_work: Maintain templates and field mappings.
Resolve missing data and failed validation.
Handle bounced messages and returned post.
Review document permissions and retention settings.
tasks.statement: Complete and mail bills, contracts, policies, invoices, or checks.

tasks.short: Prepare, copy, scan, send and store documents using office equipment.

steps.what: Retrieve electronic documents and stage them for printing or scanning.
Prepare paper, remove staples and load the scanner or copier.
Select settings and run the scanner or copier.
Check page count, legibility, orientation and completeness.
Address and send the checked document by email or fax.
Name and file the electronic copy with its delivery receipt.

tasks.design: Submit electronic originals directly from the {DOCS} or {EMAIL}, removing print-and-rescan detours. Configure scanner and copier presets in the {OTHER} office-equipment interface; a small {WORKFLOW} checks files, prepares delivery and stores receipts in the {DOCS}. The clerk handles paper, checks uncertain scans and approves external recipients.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper handling remained physical. Device settings, destinations and filing conventions differed between teams.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scan profiles and document routing handle much of this. AI-assisted coding makes small file checks and connectors cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Fragile originals, bound documents, jams and missing pages still need physical attention. Older devices may lack supported interfaces.
tasks.human_edge: Notice missing pages, protect originals and recognise when an apparently readable copy is unusable.

ambition.what: Accessible digital document packs for colleagues who struggle with paper.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer file transfers and more support for difficult documents. The clerk can choose accessible formats within agreed standards; release authority stays the same.

reach.task: Prepare searchable, correctly indexed document packs.
reach.learn: Document metadata, accessibility checks and retention schedules.

evidence.claim: Business post scanning and conversion of forms into data are available today.
Presets, file validation and routing can reduce clerical handling without a model loop.

assumptions: This models a common document-handling cycle, rather than every use of a personal computer.
The {OTHER} category covers scanner, copier and fax interfaces.
Electronic originals are available for some requests.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.
unknowns: Which devices support presets, direct storage and delivery receipts?
Which requests require physical copies or original documents?
What access, retention and recipient restrictions apply?
Do national rules require employee consultation for the proposed changes?
research_questions: Which print-and-rescan paths can disappear entirely?
Can page-count and image-quality checks catch the team's common failures?
new_work: Review flagged scans and delivery failures.
Maintain destination lists, presets and filing rules.
Test device changes and access permissions.
Apply GDPR controls to stored documents and assess any added AI use under the EU AI Act.
tasks.statement: Operate office machines, such as photocopiers and scanners, facsimile machines, voice mail systems, and personal computers.

tasks.short: Calculate office data, record results and check records or reports for errors.

steps.what: Gather source records and assemble a working data pack.
Calculate totals, dates and other required values.
Enter calculated values into the designated records or report.
Compare recorded values and report text against the source records.

loop.input: Report text, source passages and deterministic numeric check results.
loop.output: Possible wording inconsistencies with exact source references.
loop.check: Numbers and identifiers use deterministic comparisons; text flags require quoted evidence and clerk review.
loop.stop: One text-check pass per report section; unsupported flags are discarded and unresolved conflicts escalated.
loop.why_not_simpler: Formulas, schemas and spelling configuration cover mechanical checks; narrative contradictions need contextual reading.

steps.what: Resolve discrepancies and obtain approval for material corrections.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reads approved source records from the {ERP}, calculates values and validates totals without a separate working {SPREADSHEET}. It writes permitted routine updates and fills report templates in the {DOCS}; deterministic checks and a bounded text-reading loop produce a correction queue for record-owner approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual exports, repeated entry and inconsistent calculation definitions made checks slow and difficult to reproduce.
tasks.enabler_now: Direct queries, explicit formulas and repeatable validation handle structured data. AI-assisted coding reduces implementation effort, with a small reading loop for narrative checks.
tasks.still_hard: A correct calculation can still use the wrong business definition or incomplete source data. Financial postings and changes to personal records need controls matched to their consequences.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge surprising results and establish which source or business interpretation is correct.

ambition.what: Daily correction prioritisation for recurring record discrepancies.

tasks.altitude: The clerk investigates exceptions and recurring causes instead of rebuilding totals. They gain authority to prioritise the correction queue; record owners retain approval of material changes.

reach.task: Investigate recurring data-quality problems in operational reporting.
reach.learn: Control totals, reconciliation, business definitions and root-cause analysis.

evidence.claim: Rossum extracts, validates and posts invoice data to finance records, demonstrating related structured-data automation.
The documented public-health reporting failure illustrates why row counts and end-to-end control totals matter.
Calculations, field comparisons and template filling generally need deterministic code rather than model judgement.

assumptions: The baseline concerns routine office records and reports, not final payroll or payment authorisation.
Routine permitted updates are reversible and logged; material corrections require record-owner approval.
Direct source queries replace the temporary working data pack.
Build ranges cover one recurring report and one source interface, including access approval and applicable national consultation.
GDPR applies where records contain personal data; the design does not score employee performance.
unknowns: Approved calculation definitions and acceptable tolerances.
Whether source records are complete and accessible through supported interfaces.
Which updates are routine and which require material-correction approval.
Existing reconciliation controls and report-release requirements.
research_questions: Which historical errors would control totals and schema checks have caught?
Does contextual text checking find useful discrepancies beyond existing spelling and numeric checks?
new_work: Maintain calculation definitions and validation rules.
Review narrative flags and investigate unexplained totals.
Reconcile source counts with processed and written records.
Manage failed writes, changed source schemas and approved corrections.
tasks.statement: Compute, record, and proofread data and other information, such as records or reports.

tasks.short: Keep filing, stock, mailing and database records accurate and current.

steps.what: Collect record changes and supporting documents from colleagues.
Check identifiers, required fields, duplicates and supporting evidence.
Update document indexes, names, folders and filing metadata.
Enter office stock receipts, issues and location changes.
Update addresses, contact details and mailing preferences.
Copy updates into a shared tracker for cross-team reconciliation.
Count physical office stock and compare it with recorded quantities.
Investigate discrepancies and propose corrections.
Approve restricted corrections and record dispositions.
File retained paper and carry out approved physical archive changes.

tasks.design: Use structured change forms in the {WORKFLOW}, existing record controls in the {DOCS} and {CRM}, and validated stock-event integration with the {ERP}. A shared exception queue replaces the copied {SPREADSHEET} tracker, while approved corrections return to the same validated update path. People investigate discrepancies, approve restricted changes and handle physical stock and archives.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes arrived without stable identifiers or complete evidence. Separate teams maintained duplicate trackers and different validation rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms and record controls already cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of small connectors, validation and reconciliation views.
tasks.still_hard: Missing evidence cannot be created by software. Physical counts, conflicting ownership and historical duplicates need investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Find the real cause of a discrepancy and distinguish a genuine change from a mistaken or unauthorised request.

ambition.what: A weekly office-stock replenishment recommendation based on verified consumption.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time checking discrepancies and recommending replenishment, with less re-keying. They can recommend stock levels; purchasing and restricted record decisions remain with authorised roles.

reach.task: Reconcile stock movements and explain count differences.
reach.learn: Stock-event identifiers, count procedures and adjustment controls.

reach.task: Improve document indexing and retention accuracy.
reach.learn: Metadata standards, retention schedules and access classification.

evidence.claim: Structured forms, validation and record integrations can replace repeated entry without model interpretation.
A documented spreadsheet row-limit failure lost public-health records, supporting explicit completeness checks.

assumptions: The company uses the {DOCS}, {ERP} and {CRM} for the represented record types.
A shared {SPREADSHEET} tracker bridges teams despite structured source records.
These are branches of a recurring maintenance cycle, not mandatory steps for every change.
Automatic writes are limited to authorised, validated routine changes; restricted changes enter the approval queue.
The records owner is the relevant owner for each record type.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Which system is authoritative for each record type?
Are stable identifiers and supported write interfaces available?
Which tracker fields duplicate source records?
Which changes require approval, including deletion and mailing permissions?
What paper retention and national consultation rules apply?
How often do physical counts and restricted approvals occur?
research_questions: Can structured intake remove most missing-field exceptions?
Which existing record controls can replace custom code?
Can reconciliation detect missing, duplicate and partially applied changes?
new_work: Investigate rejected changes and reconciliation differences.
Maintain field mappings, validation rules and access permissions.
Check import completeness and retry failures without creating duplicates.
Keep retention and mailing-preference controls current under GDPR.
Assess EU AI Act requirements if model interpretation is later introduced.
tasks.statement: Maintain and update filing, inventory, mailing, and database systems, either manually or using a computer.

tasks.short: Handle incoming physical and electronic mail, route it, and prepare approved correspondence for dispatch.

steps.what: Receive physical post and open items permitted by handling rules.
Scan items requiring electronic circulation using the {OTHER} scanner.
Review incoming messages and attachments in the shared mailbox.
Identify recipients and handling requirements from mail content.

loop.input: Readable mail content not matched by address, sender or reference rules.
loop.output: Suggested destination queue, urgency and supporting text.
loop.check: Validate against an approved routing directory; restrict sensitive items and require clerk approval.
loop.stop: One classification attempt per unmatched item; unclear recipients and unreadable scans go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explicit addresses route deterministically; indirect references and unfamiliar correspondence require content interpretation.

steps.what: Deliver physical originals and restricted items to their recipients.
Forward electronic mail and scanned copies to the assigned recipients.
Draft routine replies using approved information and correspondence templates.

loop.input: The request, approved evidence and allowed correspondence templates.
loop.output: A draft reply with supporting references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate required fields and references; prohibit unsupported commitments and automatic sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one validation pass; missing facts produce a marked incomplete draft for human handling.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates fill standard acknowledgements; varied questions need limited wording adaptation.

steps.what: Approve routine correspondence, send electronic replies and authorise paper dispatch.
Pack, frank and dispatch approved letters using {OTHER} postal equipment.

tasks.design: Use the {WORKFLOW} to collect shared-mailbox items from the {EMAIL} and scanned copies from the {DOCS}, applying address rules before bounded content classification. Approved routing drives internal delivery, while templates and a bounded drafting loop prepare replies for human approval before external sending. Physical opening, delivery and dispatch remain with the clerk.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical handling, informal recipient knowledge and varied correspondence made the task difficult to automate as a whole.
tasks.enabler_now: Mailbox rules, scan profiles and queue routing already cover much of the paperwork. Bounded classification and drafting can support the remaining digital content steps.
tasks.still_hard: Opening restrictions, originals, ambiguous recipients and postal handling remain. GDPR requires careful routing and limited retention of sensitive correspondence.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise sensitive or unusual correspondence and choose an appropriate response or escalation.

ambition.what: A deadline alert service for time-sensitive incoming correspondence.

tasks.altitude: The clerk still handles physical mail and approves outgoing replies, but spends less time forwarding and typing. They can prioritise overdue internal routing under an agreed escalation policy; authority to make external commitments does not expand.

reach.task: Resolve recurring failures in mail delivery and response handling.
reach.learn: Queue design, service deadlines and confidential-mail procedures.

evidence.claim: PostNL offers business-post scanning and conversion of forms into data.
Paperbox organises insurance mail into case files, supporting the digital routing component.
A documented insurance case reports automation of over 60% of claims correspondence; this is not a general-office forecast.

assumptions: This baseline has substantial physical post; a mostly digital office would have a different time split.
Only post approved for scanning is digitised.
The clerk may approve routine factual replies; commitments and specialist matters go to authorised roles.
Build ranges cover one mailroom and one shared mailbox, with applicable national consultation and access approval.
No employee-level productivity scoring is included.
unknowns: Physical and electronic mail volumes and existing scanning arrangements.
Which items must remain unopened or retain physical originals.
Current recipient directory quality and correspondence approval limits.
Which messages carry statutory or contractual deadlines.
Applicable national rules for employee consultation.
research_questions: Which routing errors would disclose sensitive information, and can rules reliably exclude those items?
How much correspondence can approved templates answer without a model?
new_work: Review uncertain routing suggestions and unreadable scans.
Maintain recipient mappings, templates and deadline rules.
Check draft replies before external sending.
Monitor failed deliveries and duplicate routing.
tasks.statement: Open, sort, and route incoming mail, answer correspondence, and prepare outgoing mail.

tasks.short: Find and verify information in office records to support responses to requests.

steps.what: Read the request and clarify the information needed.
Search folders and record screens for relevant sources.
Read sources and compile relevant facts with references.

loop.input: The request brief and permission-filtered source passages.
loop.output: Relevant facts with source locations, dates and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Require a source for every factual statement; verify references and flag conflicting versions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one validation pass over at most 20 passages; unresolved questions go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact identifiers support ordinary lookup, but narrative documents express relevant facts in varied language.

steps.what: Check completeness and disclosure permission before handing over findings.

tasks.design: Configure permission-filtered search across the {DOCS} and approved records from the {ERP}. A bounded reading loop assembles cited findings in the {WORKFLOW}; the clerk checks gaps and obtains record-owner approval where disclosure needs authorisation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information sat in disconnected folders and record screens, with inconsistent references and uncertain versions.
tasks.enabler_now: Search configuration and approved record views cover exact lookups. Bounded reading can assemble evidence from narrative sources without granting wider access.
tasks.still_hard: Missing records and contradictory accounts cannot be solved by search alone. Permission to read a source does not automatically permit disclosure to the requester.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the real question, notice misleading context and explain uncertainty to the requester.

ambition.what: A cited records lookup service for colleagues working outside office hours.

tasks.altitude: The clerk reviews evidence and pursues gaps instead of repeatedly opening files. They can fulfil approved routine internal lookups directly; sensitive disclosure rights remain with record owners.

reach.task: Assemble evidence for a recurring operational problem.
reach.learn: Source evaluation, version control and separating facts from interpretations.

evidence.claim: Permission-filtered retrieval and cited extraction can support routine record enquiries; applicability depends on source quality.
The digest supports an answer desk using approved policy text and record status, with unknowns referred to people.

assumptions: The task ends with verified findings; sending the final response belongs to the request owner.
The baseline covers office documents and finance-related record lookups, not unrestricted access to employee files.
Existing search can enforce source permissions; otherwise integration scope increases.
Build ranges cover one document collection and one approved record view, including applicable national consultation.
GDPR access and purpose limits apply; employment-decision uses require a separate EU AI Act assessment.
unknowns: Which request types are common and who may receive each information category.
Whether source permissions and current versions are reliable.
Whether the existing search supports the required record views.
Required response languages, service hours and disclosure approval rules.
research_questions: How often does a cited answer omit a material qualification in the source?
What proportion of requests can exact lookup resolve before narrative reading is needed?
new_work: Review source citations and unresolved contradictions.
Maintain approved source collections and access mappings.
Test retrieval after permission or document-structure changes.
Turn repeated unanswered questions into requests for better records.
tasks.statement: Review files, records, and other documents to obtain information to respond to requests.

tasks.short: Relay messages and carry out practical office errands.

steps.what: Receive the request and clarify its purpose, urgency, and handling needs.
Find the recipient, destination, contact details, and access arrangements.
Write an errand list and fit trips around deadlines and other duties.
Walk to a coworker and relay a routine message.
Collect the physical item and check handling instructions.
Travel to the destination, complete the errand, and hand over the item.
Tell the requester the outcome or explain an unsuccessful handover.

tasks.design: Configure a request queue in {WORKFLOW}, using directory data from {HCM} and {DOCS} to populate destinations and group trips.
